ka-script-1.title: The Georgian Alphabet: Vowels
ka-script-1.pattern: ა a · ე e · ი i · ო o · უ u
ka-script-1.explanation: Georgian is written in its own alphabet, Mkhedruli (მხედრული): 33 letters, written left to right. There are no capital letters, and every letter always has the same sound, so once you know the letters you can read any word aloud. Start with the five vowels: ა (a as in 'father'), ე (e as in 'bed'), ი (i as in 'machine'), ო (o as in 'more'), უ (u as in 'rule'). With them come მ (m) and დ (d): დედა is 'mother' and მამა is 'father'.
ka-script-1.fact: Georgian is one of only a handful of languages in the world with its own unique alphabet, and the script is on UNESCO's list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

ka-script-2.title: The Alphabet: Familiar Consonants
ka-script-2.pattern: ბ b · გ g · ვ v · ზ z · ლ l · ნ n · რ r · ს s · ჰ h
ka-script-2.explanation: Many Georgian consonants sound just like their English equivalents: ბ (b), გ (always hard g, as in 'go'), ვ (v), ზ (z), ლ (l), ნ (n), ს (s), ჰ (h). რ is a rolled or tapped r, as in Spanish or Russian. Notice how many letters are round and rest on the line, with some reaching above (ბ, ლ) or below (გ, ვ). Also learn the short copula -ა: instead of saying ეს სახლი არის ('this is a house'), Georgians usually say ეს სახლია. A word ending in -ი drops it (სახლი → სახლია); a word ending in another vowel just adds -ა (გოგო → გოგოა).
ka-script-2.fact: Georgian has no grammatical gender at all: the same word ის means 'he', 'she' and 'it', and adjectives never change for masculine or feminine.

ka-script-3.title: Aspirated vs Ejective Consonants
ka-script-3.pattern: თ t / ტ t' · ქ k / კ k' · ფ p / პ p'
ka-script-3.explanation: This is the heart of Georgian pronunciation. Georgian has two kinds of t, k and p. The aspirated ones, თ (t), ქ (k), ფ (p), are said with a small puff of air, like English 'top', 'kite', 'pen'. The ejective ones, ტ (t'), კ (k'), პ (p'), have no puff: close your throat briefly and release the sound with a sharp click-like pop. The transliteration marks ejectives with an apostrophe. The difference changes meanings, so listen to the audio and imitate it.
ka-script-3.fact: Georgian is famous for long clusters of consonants. The word გვფრცქვნი ('you peel us') has eight consonants in a row and no vowel until the very end.

ka-script-4.title: Affricates: ც წ ძ ჩ ჭ ჯ
ka-script-4.pattern: ც ts / წ ts' · ჩ ch / ჭ ch' · ძ dz · ჯ j
ka-script-4.explanation: Affricates are sounds that start like a stop and end like a hiss. They come in the same aspirated/ejective pairs: ც (ts, as in 'cats') vs წ (ts', ejective), ჩ (ch, as in 'church') vs ჭ (ch', ejective). ძ is dz as in 'adze', and ჯ is j as in 'jam'. წყალი ('water') starts with an ejective ts' followed by q', a hard pair to say, so practise it slowly.
ka-script-4.fact: The word for 'water', წყალი, is one of the first words learners practise because it combines two ejective sounds in a row.

dialogue.en: Yes, the water is very cold.

ka-script-5.title: Back of the Throat: ღ ყ ხ, plus შ ჟ
ka-script-5.pattern: ხ kh · ღ gh · ყ q' · შ sh · ჟ zh
ka-script-5.explanation: Georgian has several sounds made far back in the mouth. ხ (kh) is a rough h, like the ch in Scottish 'loch'. ღ (gh) is its voiced partner, a soft gargled sound similar to a French r. ყ (q') is an ejective made even deeper in the throat than კ. Two easier ones: შ (sh as in 'shop') and ჟ (zh, like the s in 'pleasure').
ka-script-5.fact: Georgian cheese bread, ხაჭაპური (khachap'uri), contains three of the trickiest sounds in one word: ხ, ჭ and პ.

ka-script-6.title: Reading Whole Words
ka-script-6.explanation: You now know all 33 letters. Because Georgian spelling is perfectly regular, reading is simply sounding out each letter in order. Stress is light and usually falls on the first syllable, so don't stress the last syllable as in Russian or Spanish. Practise with the most useful words of all: გამარჯობა (hello), მადლობა (thank you), ბოდიში (sorry), ნახვამდის (goodbye).
ka-script-6.fact: გამარჯობა ('hello') literally means 'victory'. The reply, გაგიმარჯოს, means 'may you be victorious'.
